description: Two-operator oscillator built from toroidal orbit equations, a little circle winding around a big one, with the X, Y and Z of the traced path as three outputs and a distortion stage on each

params.text: Sets the frequency of the big circle, -60 to 60 semitones around 130.813Hz
Sets the frequency of the little circle, -60 to 60 semitones around 130.813Hz
Chooses the orbit equation, Electron, Folded or Toroidal from the bottom position upwards
Divides the little circle's frequency by 1024, ten octaves down, which turns it into a slow modulator
Divides the big circle's frequency by 1024, ten octaves down, which turns it into a slow modulator
Sets how many times the path goes round the big circle in one cycle, 1 to 6, though the value is clamped at 5, so the top of the travel does nothing
Sets how many times the path goes round the little circle in one cycle, 1 to 6, though the value is clamped at 5, so the top of the travel does nothing
Multiplies the PM input, -1 to 1; with no cable in the PM jack the knob is used on its own, which shifts both circles slightly in frequency
Sets how much smaller the little circle is than the big one, which is fixed at 45 units; a negative setting makes the little circle the larger of the two
Sets how hard the three outputs are driven, 0 to 11; with a cable in the Drive jack this knob scales that voltage instead
Chooses the distortion applied to all three outputs: a warm saturation, eight stages of wavefolding, or hard clipping, from the bottom position upwards
Adds the big circle's pitch to the little circle's, so the little circle tracks the big one and the Little Pitch controls become an interval
Spreads four copies of the whole orbit apart in pitch, up to about a third of a semitone either way, and all four are added together at the outputs

inputs.text: Added to the Big Pitch knob at one volt per octave
Added to the Little Pitch knob at one volt per octave
Added to the Big Windings knob, one winding per volt; the absolute value of the total is taken and clamped to 5
Added to the Little Windings knob, one winding per volt; the absolute value of the total is taken and clamped to 5
Phase modulation for both circles, multiplied by the PM knob and added to both phases every sample
Scaled to -10 to 45 and added to the Radius knob, the total clamped to that span; a positive voltage shrinks the little circle, which is why the hover text calls it inverted
The absolute value of the voltage, times a fifth of the Drive knob, replaces the knob's own setting
A rise above 0V restarts both circles at the start of their cycles

outputs.text: The horizontal axis of the chosen orbit equation, after the distortion stage
The vertical axis of the chosen orbit equation, after the distortion stage
The depth axis of the chosen orbit equation, after the distortion stage

notes: four copies of the orbit run at once and are added together at the outputs; with Detune at the centre all four are identical
the screen draws the path the orbit traces, which is what the three outputs are the coordinates of
every output is monophonic, whatever is patched in
